en: Now, the last core feature that's worth
mentioning is that Bunsen's S3 client also
supports presigned URLs. And what are
presigned URLs? Well, that bucket here is
private by default. For all storage
providers I know, buckets are private by
default. You can see public access is
disabled. So I can view it here because I'm
logged in. I can interact with it through
that CLI because of those env vars I
defined.
But if I gave you
a link to that bucket, however that would
look like, you wouldn't be able to do
anything with it.
But what if I want to share that file with
you, a file in the cloud? What if I wanted
to share that with you?
That is where presigned URLs come into play.
You can create a short-lived URL that points
at a certain file in a private bucket and
make that file if you have that URL,
not private, as long as that URL is valid.
And that's what the share feature in this
CLI is about. In there, in this share.ts
file, in the share function, I'm using the
presign method on that S3 client. So still
the same Bun S3 client, but now using
presign
to point at a key, so the path of a file on
And then configure that URL I wanna create.
For example, I say that the method will be
GET, so it will only be valid for reading
that file, not for overwriting it. We could
also use the method PUT if we wanted someone
else to have a URL they can use for
replacing that file, but I only want GET.
I have expiresIn, which is an input I expect
to get here,
and that's coming from index.ts.
It's there where we have share
And there we set a default
of 3,600 seconds.
And then also some extra details about the
filename that should be used for downloading
that file, for example.
And you can see that feature in action if I
run bun run cli share
and then I provide that remote key, that
remote filename.
So if I run bun run cli list, I see all the
files I have remotely and now I can share,
let's say this file
Like this, and I get back a URL. And if I
now copy that URL and I open a new
incognito browser window where I'm not
logged in, I can insert that URL and view
that file,
but only for an hour. Thereafter, this link
will no longer work.
But that's of course also a nice useful
feature and Bun has built-in support for it
out of the box.
